title: False Frontiers: Diagnosing and Mitigating Co-Cheating in Self-Evolving Search Agents
title_zh: 虚假前沿：诊断与缓解自进化搜索智能体中的协同作弊
abstract_en: Self-evolving search agents build their own training curricula by jointly optimizing a proposer that generates questions and a solver that answers them. This closed loop introduces a failure mode we call co-cheating: the proposer and solver increasingly agree on shared errors, so internal reward improves without a matching gain in external correctness. A post-hoc audit against source evidence shows co-cheating growing more severe over successive rounds of self-evolution, with pseudo-label correctness stagnating or declining even as the in-loop training signal improves. The most direct mitigation is to verify proposals before training: we introduce multi-sample verification (MSV), which queries the same model three times with the source and three times without it to decide task admission and replace unreliable pseudo-labels. MSV partially reduces false agreement but leaves substantial residual co-cheating and costs six extra labeler generations per candidate. These limitations motivate CrossFit, our main method: it partitions the proposer's source documents into groups A and B; questions generated from A are scored by an auxiliary solver trained only on B, and vice versa. The cross-fitted agreement determines proposer reward, so a same-source pseudo-label cannot be reproduced through the feedback solver, while the original solver's update rule is unchanged. Rerunning the loop with Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.5-9B, MSV reduces false-agreement mass from 6.1% to 5.7% and from 8.8% to 7.2%, whereas CrossFit reduces it to 3.0% and 3.7%. Replaying identical proposals with source-excluded feedback further reduces false agreement to 0.4% and 0.1%, isolating feedback ancestry from curriculum changes. Across seven downstream search benchmarks, CrossFit improves average performance over standard coupled self-evolution by 8.8 and 8.4 points and over Search-R1 by 8.7 and 7.8 points at 4B and 9B.
abstract_zh: 自进化搜索智能体通过联合优化提问生成器（proposer）与问题求解器（solver）构建训练课程，但这一闭环会产生“协同作弊”（co-cheating）：二者逐渐共享并强化错误，使内部奖励提升却不代表外部正确性改善。基于源证据的事后审计表明，随着自进化轮次增加，协同作弊愈发严重，伪标签正确率停滞甚至下降。作者首先提出多样本验证（Multi-Sample Verification, MSV），通过分别在有源和无源条件下对同一模型采样三次，筛选任务并替换不可靠伪标签；但其只能部分缓解问题，且每个候选任务额外消耗六次生成。核心方法 CrossFit 将提问生成器的源文档划分为 A、B 两组：A 生成的问题由仅使用 B 训练的辅助求解器评分，B 生成的问题则反向评分，以交叉拟合的一致性决定 proposer 奖励，从而阻断反馈求解器复现同源伪标签的路径，同时保持原 solver 的更新规则不变。在 Qwen3.5-4B 和 Qwen3.5-9B 上，CrossFit 将虚假一致性比例分别降至 3.0% 和 3.7%，优于 MSV 的 5.7% 和 7.2%；在七个下游搜索基准上，相比标准耦合式自进化，平均性能分别提升 8.8 和 8.4 个百分点，相比 Search-R1 分别提升 8.7 和 7.8 个百分点。
key_points_zh: 自进化搜索的 proposer 与 solver 会共享错误，导致内部奖励上升但外部正确性不变甚至下降。
MSV通过有源和无源多次采样验证候选任务，可部分缓解协同作弊，但计算开销高且残留问题明显。
CrossFit将源文档分组，并用仅见另一组文档训练的辅助 solver 进行交叉评分，切断同源伪标签的反馈路径。
在 Qwen3.5-4B/9B 上，CrossFit将虚假一致性降至3.0%/3.7%，显著优于MSV的5.7%/7.2%。
在七个搜索基准上，CrossFit相较标准耦合式自进化平均提升8.8/8.4个百分点，相较Search-R1提升8.7/7.8个百分点。

llm_assessment.comment: The paper identifies a fundamental failure mode in self-evolving search agents and supplies a cross-fitted feedback mechanism with strong downstream evidence.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: 论文揭示了自演化搜索Agent中的根本性失效模式，并提出了具有较强下游效果证据的交叉拟合反馈机制。
